channel.title: Oui Academy Blog
channel.description: Pronunciation tips, real DELF/DALF/TCF exam experience, and practical French learning advice.

item.title: TCF Canada Test Day: What to Bring and How Early to Arrive
item.description: It's a computer-based test, not paper — getting comfortable with the interface beforehand saves time you'd otherwise lose fumbling through it on test day. What to bring, when to arrive, and the small details that cause problems on site.

item.title: How to Actually Remember French Vocabulary Long-Term (Spaced Repetition)
item.description: Learning 50 words in one sitting, then forgetting most of them a week later, isn't a memory problem — it's a review-timing problem. Spaced repetition and how to apply it without a complicated app.

item.title: 9 Common Irregular French Verbs You'll Need for TCF Canada
item.description: Être, avoir, aller, faire... show up in almost every sentence you speak or write, no matter the topic. Getting these wrong stands out far more than a rare verb — present-tense forms and real examples.

item.title: The Complete TCF Canada Guide
item.description: 20 articles on TCF Canada, organized in the order you should actually read them — from picking the right certificate, to exam structure, skill-by-skill practice, registration, and using your score.

item.title: How Do You Know You're Ready for TCF Canada?
item.description: Confidence isn't a reliable signal. A 5-question practical checklist to assess yourself before registering, instead of waiting for a feeling of certainty that may never come.

item.title: Where to Listen to Free French Every Day
item.description: There's no shortage of free French content online — the issue is usually picking the wrong level of source. How to choose free daily listening content without getting discouraged by material that's too hard or too easy.

item.title: Useful Connectors for TCF Canada Speaking and Writing
item.description: Same argument, more coherent delivery when connectors land in the right place. A list organized by function — adding, contrasting, cause, conclusion — and how to use them naturally, not stiffly.

item.title: You've Got Your TCF Canada Score — What's Next?
item.description: Your score is one piece of an Express Entry application, not the finish line. How the result gets converted, factored into your CRS score, and what to do right after you receive it.

item.title: TCF Canada vs. TCF Québec: What's the Difference?
item.description: Two similar-sounding names that serve two different immigration systems — one for federal applications, one for Québec's own programs. Register for the wrong version and the result won't count.

item.title: A Daily French Practice Habit for Busy Schedules
item.description: 15 consistent minutes a day beats 3 hours on the weekend. How to build a realistic daily French habit for people with packed schedules, without needing extra free time.

item.title: TCF Canada Fees and How to Register
item.description: Where to register, what documents you need, and why you should lock in a test date before you feel "ready." The TCF Canada registration process and the details people miss.

item.title: TCF Canada Speaking: Strategy for the Most Feared Section
item.description: 12 minutes, 3 tasks, no preparation time — you draw a topic and speak immediately. The Speaking section's structure, the mistake that gets low scores, and how to train reflexes instead of memorizing scripts.

item.title: How Long Is TCF Canada Valid? Timing Your Test for an Immigration Application
item.description: IRCC only accepts TCF Canada results within 2 years of the test date — testing too early relative to your filing date is just as risky as testing too late. How to work backward to the right test date.

item.title: How Far Ahead Should You Start Prepping for TCF Canada?
item.description: Cramming right before an Express Entry deadline is the most common recipe for a low score and a retake. How to plan backward from the NCLC level you need, so you're not scrambling at the last minute.

item.title: Knowing Grammar and Being Able to Speak Are Two Different Things
item.description: You can conjugate correctly on paper and remember every gender rule, yet freeze when asked to answer out loud. That's not a grammar problem — it's a missing skill entirely: speaking reflex.

item.title: What Is the French Club, and Who Should Join?
item.description: One small-group live session a week, topics prepared by level, EUR15/month with no long-term commitment. What the French Club is, who it's for, and why speaking with other people beats practicing alone.

item.title: How Is DALF C1/C2 Different from DELF B1/B2, and Do You Really Need It?
item.description: DELF stops at B2, DALF starts at C1 — the difference isn't just harder, the whole nature of the exam changes. When you actually need DALF, and when B2 is already enough.

item.title: Record and Compare: The Simplest Pronunciation Self-Review Tool
item.description: The step most self-learners skip when working on pronunciation: listening back to their own voice. How to record and compare effectively, and why this step matters more than most people think.

item.title: 5 French Grammar Mistakes Vietnamese Speakers Make (and How to Fix Them)
item.description: Vietnamese doesn't conjugate verbs, doesn't mark grammatical gender, and has no concept of a fixed preposition tied to a verb — the root of the same grammar mistakes repeating for years. 5 common mistakes and how to fix each one.

item.title: TCF Canada Reading: Reading Fast and Accurately Under Time Pressure
item.description: 60 minutes for 39 questions, from short simple sentences to complex argumentative passages. Time-management strategy, correct reading pace, and the mistake that makes most people run out of time.

item.title: TCF Canada Listening: How Do You Train for a No-Replay Exam?
item.description: 39 multiple-choice questions, increasing difficulty, no replays — TCF Canada Listening needs a different strategy than ordinary listening practice. How to train so you don't run out of steam mid-exam.

item.title: Retaking TCF Canada: How Long Should You Wait, and Is There a Limit?
item.description: There's no cap on how many times you can retake TCF Canada, but retaking too soon without fixing the actual weak point just costs more time and money. How to know when you're actually ready to retake.

item.title: How Is Quebec French Different from Standard French?
item.description: You train in standard French for TCF/TEF, then land in Quebec and hear a completely different accent. The real differences in pronunciation and vocabulary, and why standard French still comes first.

item.title: TCF Canada Writing Section: 3 Task Types and How to Score High
item.description: The TCF Canada Writing section has 3 independent tasks, each graded on its own criteria. Structure of each task type, mistakes that cost the most points, and how to practice correctly.

item.title: TCF Canada Vocabulary by Topic: The 4 Most Common Groups
item.description: TCF Canada is built around real-life situations, not random word lists. The 4 most common vocabulary topics on the exam, concrete examples, and how to make them stick.

item.title: TCF Canada Exam Structure: 4 Skills and How NCLC Scoring Works
item.description: TCF Canada has no overall pass/fail — Listening, Reading, Speaking, and Writing are each scored independently and converted to the NCLC scale. Exam structure and how to plan your prep time.

item.title: What Is Shadowing and Why Does It Speed Up Spoken French?
item.description: Shadowing — listening and repeating almost simultaneously — is a speaking-reflex technique used in interpreter training. How to practice it correctly, common mistakes, and why immediate feedback matters.

item.title: Learning French for Canadian Immigration: A Complete Guide to TCF/TEF and the Method That Works
item.description: A complete guide: why French strengthens an Express Entry application, TCF vs TEF, the NCLC scale, and the modern method for training the exact skills the exam grades.

item.title: DELF B2 Exam Structure and Tips to Score High
item.description: DELF B2 has 4 independent sections worth 25 points each — but passing depends on each section, not just the total. Full breakdown and tips per skill.

item.title: TCF Canada: How Many Points Do You Need for Immigration?
item.description: TCF Canada doesn't grade pass/fail by level like DELF — it converts each skill onto the NCLC scale. Understand the score bands that actually matter for Express Entry.

item.title: TCF Canada vs. TEF Canada: Which Should You Take?
item.description: Both are accepted by IRCC for Express Entry, but they differ in who administers them and the exam format. Know the difference before you register.

item.title: Can You Self-Study for DELF/DALF, or Do You Need a Tutor?
item.description: Grammar and vocabulary, you can self-study. But two skills almost always plateau without help — here's how to tell which stage you're in.

item.title: DELF, DALF, TCF Canada: Which Exam Should You Take?
item.description: The three most confused names in French certification — what separates them, which one expires, and how to pick the right one for study, work, or Canadian immigration.

item.title: How Long Does It Take to Go From A1 to B2?
item.description: Real session counts from A1 to B2, and the factors that decide whether you move fast or slow — a straight answer to the question everyone asks before starting.

item.title: 5 French Pronunciation Mistakes Vietnamese Speakers Make (and How to Fix Them)
item.description: From the hard-to-tell-apart 'u' sound to the back-of-throat 'r' and liaison — the 5 most common French pronunciation mistakes for Vietnamese speakers, and how to actually fix them.
